title: Explicit trust boundary terminates verification regress
problem: Recursively asking who verifies each verifier creates an infinite regress unless the assurance case declares a trust boundary.
rules: Every primitive evidence node must map to exactly one explicit trust root.
Every trust root must state at least one assumption.
Missing or duplicate root identities make the trust boundary incomplete.
Trust roots are exposed assumptions, not silently promoted proofs.
invariants: Verification Regress Must Terminate in Declared Assumptions
boundary: This contract makes trust assumptions inspectable. It does not establish that a declared trust root is reliable.
